provisions.summary: Renewable energy technologies credit: aggregate annual cap of $40M for 2027-2030, $0 from 2031
Renewable energy technologies credit limited to taxpayers with AGI up to $175,000 (individual) or $350,000 (joint)
provisions.quote: provided that the taxpayer's adjusted gross income does not exceed $175,000 if filing as an individual, or $350,000 if filing jointly

provisions.summary: Renewable energy technologies credit sunsets for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2029
provisions.quote: This section shall not apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2029.

provisions.summary: Repeals the scheduled 2027 and 2029 bracket adjustments and enacts new schedules for 2027 and 2029 (new 2.5% and 5.0% rates, new 13% top rate) for joint, head of household and single filers
Capital goods excise tax credit sunsets for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2027
provisions.quote: This section shall not apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2027.

provisions.summary: Renewable fuels production tax credit sunsets for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2028
provisions.quote: This section shall not apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2028.

provisions.summary: Repeals the high technology business investment tax credit effective January 1, 2029
provisions.quote: Section 235-110.9, Hawaii Revised Statutes, is repealed.

provisions.summary: Repeals the technology infrastructure renovation tax credit effective January 1, 2028
provisions.quote: Section 235-110.51, Hawaii Revised Statutes, is repealed.

provisions.summary: Moves up the effective date of Act 261 (2019) Part II (the research activities credit repeal, per the bill description) from January 1, 2030 to January 1, 2029
provisions.quote: Part II shall take effect on [January 1, 2030.] January 1, 2029.

notes: Spec contains only the bracket schedules; standard deduction, exemption, capital gains rate and credits are unchanged from current law (Act 24, SLH 2026), and Act 163's sunset is untouched. Section 2 brackets are the unbracketed schedules for years after 12/31/2026 (new rates) and after 12/31/2028; the bracketed older 2027 and 2028 schedules are repealed. Married filing separately uses the single schedule. No schedule changes after 2029. Section 1's renewable energy credit has an internal inconsistency: subsection (c)(5) sets the cap to $0 beginning January 1, 2031 while new subsection (p) ends the section after taxable years beginning December 31, 2029, so the credit ends after 2029 on its face, while the $40M cap is stated for 2030. Section 1's AGI limit applies from tax years after 12/31/2026, and the rest of section 1 applies retroactively to tax years after 12/31/2025. The high technology business investment credit (section 235-110.9) and technology infrastructure renovation credit (section 235-110.51) already carry their own sunsets for taxable years after 12/31/2010, so their repeals may have little or no fiscal effect. The research credit repeal in section 7 changes only a date in the Act 261 amendment; the credit itself is not named in the bill text. None of the credit provisions can be expressed in the spec. Effective-date section 9 sets section 5 effective 1/1/2029 and section 6 effective 1/1/2028; sections 2-4 apply to tax years after 12/31/2026.
